messages:
maria: quick status — trying to finish cedar-lite-7b onboarding, hitting a licensing nuance. pinging legal for quick triage.

maria: summary: model tarball and manifest uploaded, perf profiles attached, but LICENSE file says CC-BY-NC-4.0 (non-commercial). we need guidance for hosted + dedicated.

maria: manifest snippet pasted: ```name: cedar-lite-7b
source: hf://open/cedar-lite
version: v1.0.0
license: CC-BY-NC-4.0
sha256: 3a7f6c...```

lee: thanks — looking. is the license file exactly that or are there embedded clarifications? also: who requested this model?

maria: curator request from @sasha/product; ingest link: https://storage.redwood.internal/models/cedar-lite/v1/manifest.json

lee: NC clause is a blocker for any commercial-facing hosted offering. for internal/demos it's usually ok. if product wants this available to paying customers we need either a different license or an exception via legal review + risk doc.

sasha: product note — folks asked for cedar-lite because it has stronger instruction-following than cedar-compat. if NC means no paid customers, product impact is moderate. can we gate it to free-tier only or dedicated private instances?

josh: from infra side — perf baseline done on A100-80k, int8 path. numbers: 0.32s/token avg, 18 tokens/ms throughput on 2xA100. memory grows ~0.5GB per 1k context due to kv-cache. quant profile q4_1 stable for inference; q4_0 had output noise in long contexts.

ara: QA quick note — eval suite (small prompt set) shows a +3% hallucination delta vs cedar-compat on our safety prompts. samples in #evals.

sasha: can we mitigate safety regressions with prompt templates or rerankers? if we plan fallback routing to cedar-compat for paid routes, product OK. need cost/latency delta.

josh: delta: cedar-compat is ~8% slower and ~12% cheaper (less memory, different tokenizer). fallback is feasible. I'll prototype routing weights and a canary.

maria: proposed plan: 1) lee confirm licensing policy + whether exception possible by Thu noon; 2) josh prepare canary routing config and fallback to cedar-compat for paid routes; 3) ara run failover evals and post metrics; 4) legal-bot create ticket. target: finish by EOW.

legal-bot: Created LEG-2042: "Cedar-lite-7b license exception request" — assigned to @lee.

josh: opened draft PR for routing rules: https://git.redwood/infra/routing/pull/128 — adds route for model=cedar-lite-7b with fallback to cedar-compat-7b under paid_tier. includes metric hooks for latency and quality-drift.

maria: @josh drop the example canary config inline? small snippet is fine.

josh: snippet: ```canary: true
canary_pool: dedicated-west-1
traffic_split: {free_tier: 100, paid_tier: 0} # initial
override_on_ok: {paid_tier: 90 -> cedar-lite-7b}```

sasha: product ok with that as long as we track prompt-quality and error-rate. add dashboard tile for drift.

ara: will add eval run id: eval/cedar-lite-202603-01 and baseline id cedar-compat-202602. I'll post the result snapshot here when done.

lee: quick update — reading license and reach-out to upstream for commercial clarification. if upstream denies commercial, recommend restricting cedar-lite to non-paid tiers and private deployments. will confirm by Thu.

maria: thanks. timeline check — if legal says restrict, we proceed with canary on free tier and add explicit route guards. if allowed, we'll expand to paid after contractual sign-off.

ingest-bot: Model ingest complete: cedar-lite-7b v1.0.0 (sha256:3a7f6c...). Size: 13.9GB compressed.

maria: good catch. anyone object to schedule a small canary Wed morning on dedicated-west-1 free pool?

sasha: fine from product.

josh: scheduling it now. I'll post the canary runbook and smoke tests.

lee: will post legal gameplan by Thu 12:00.

maria: thanks all — i'll update the onboarding tracker and close out once LEG-2042 resolved and QA pass. cc @sasha @josh @ara
